title: Surya Namaskar Is Not Ancient | Challenge and Win Rs 200,000
tags: Bala Sahib Pant Pratinidhi Surya Namaskar
description:
Every year, millions celebrate International Yoga Day believing yoga is an ancient Indian tradition handed down from sages. But the truth is very different. Modern yoga — the asanas and postures you see in gyms, schools, and studios — is a recent invention.

Take Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation). People think it’s an ancient practice, but it was actually created by Bala Sahib Pant Pratinidhi, the Raja of Aundh, in the early 20th century. Inspired by European bodybuilding legend Eugene Sandow, he developed it as a fitness routine — not a spiritual practice. Later, it was popularized by figures like Krishnamacharya and B.K.S. Iyengar.

Or consider Shirshasana (headstand). Branded the “King of Asanas,” it is often claimed to be described in ancient yogic texts. Yet no classical yoga scripture mentions it. In fact, most yoga poses seen today were invented in the 19th and 20th centuries, not by rishis of the past.

Orthopaedic surgeon and rationalist Visvanathan C has even thrown open two public challenges:

₹1 lakh to anyone who can prove Surya Namaskar existed in yoga texts before Raja Pant Pratinidhi.
₹1 lakh to anyone who can prove Shirshasana existed in yoga texts before the 19th century.
So far, no one has claimed these prizes — because the evidence simply doesn’t exist.

If you’ve searched for truth about yoga, modern yoga origins, Surya Namaskar history, Shirshasana fact check, or Yoga Day exposed, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Like, comment, share, and hype this video so more people see through the myths and understand the real history of yoga.
